# Phase Two — Improved Architecture

The Awtsmoos is One while responsibilities divide so each can be clear,
Awtsmoos.com will keep the Shliach campaign modular, fast, and easy to steer.

## Chosen architecture
Use the repository static-route convention. HTML owns content and SEO; shared CSS owns identity and motion; tiny browser-native ESM owns only prompt launching and optional reveal effects. No framework, build system, or new server dependency will appear.

## Homepage repair
Rewrite `ShliachSpotlightContent.js` in full. The public Drive logo becomes primary. If it fails, the existing `/resources/branding/awtsmoos-shliach-agent.png` is tried before the text fallback appears. Copy gains a clear internal campaign link while retaining an unmistakable external “Open actual Shliach” action.

## Campaign routes
`/Shliach/` answers “what is it?” and offers the prompt launcher immediately.
`/Shliach/prompts/` answers “what should I ask?” with useful starter prompts.
`/Shliach/poems/` answers the literary identity side with original rhyming work and visual art.
`/Shliach/gallery/` answers visual discovery with bridge and coder-portal imagery plus meaningful captions.

## Shared visual system
A small import file composes tokens, foundation, navigation, hero, sections, prompt, motion, and responsive modules. Imagery carries broad gradients and light without making text depend on image contrast. Motion remains transform/opacity based where possible.

## Browser behavior
`ShliachPaths.js` builds the destination from one exact GPT base URL. `OhrPromptPortal.js` binds every `[data-shliach-prompt-form]`, validates non-empty input, and opens the encoded URL from the user submit gesture. `ChesedRevealOrchestrator.js` adds optional intersection classes but reveals content immediately when observation is unavailable or reduced motion is requested.

## Verification after source pass
Run the existing Home contract; add and run a new campaign contract; syntax-check every new JS module; enforce <=120 lines for touched source files; inspect public image/GPT HTTP paths; preview all four pages at desktop/mobile widths; submit a Unicode prompt and confirm the outbound URL carries the full encoded value.
